newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ building consents up 13.5 pct in November year.
newsitem.headline: NZ building consents up 13.5 pct in November year.

text.p: The total value of building consents for the November year was $6.14 billion, up 13.5 percent on the November 1995 year, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
That compared with $6.12 billion, up 12.7 percent in the October 1996 year.

For non-residential buildings, consents with a total value of NZ$2.52 billion were authorised in the year ended November, a rise of 18.7 percent from the year ended November 1995. That compares with $2.53 billion in the October year.
Non-residential consents in the month of November were valued at $191.8 million against the November 1995 figure of $198.4 million.
The value of consents for residential buildings in November rose 9.1 percent to $334 million from November 1995. Consents in November 1995 were valued at $310.1 million.
The national median consent value for new dwelling units authorised inNovember was $120,000, an increase of 1.2 percent over November 1995.
